newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Safeway labor talks stalled again.
newsitem.headline: Canada Safeway labor talks stalled again.

text.p: Canada Safeway Ltd said negoiations with leaders of its striking unions in Alberta, which resumed on May 8, stalled with no agreement being hammered out.

Canada Safeway, whose unionized grocery clerks, meat cutters and bakers at 74 stores in the western Canadian province walked off the job in late March, said mediation and an amended offer to employees yielded no deal to end the dispute.

"We returned to the table with a goal of getting our people back to work as soon as possible, and made significant moves on our position in order to accomplish that end," Grant Hansen, Canada Safeway's president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
"We are disappointed that the talks have ended without a settlement."
Mediated talks between the unions, led by the United Food and Commercial workers, and Canada Safeway, a unit of Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway Inc, proceeded for 10 days.

The company said its amended offer addressed several issues highlighted by the unions, and included offers to guarantee minimum hours for part-time employees and match top wage rates unions were able to wrest from its chief Alberta competitor, the Real Canadian Superstore.
Hansen said, however, the company's main concern was that Superstore, a unit of Loblaw Cos Ltd, had given its unionized staff lower wage rates and progressions than Safeway.
"We must have parity in this area if we are to remain competitive," Hansen said.
No new talks had been scheduled. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
